data.summary: publish #34 mcp-registry job: registry returned 422, body.description expected length <= 100; server.json description is 251 chars (since 7b9aed8). 0.1.3 reached PyPI and GHCR but not the MCP Registry, and the tag job did not run. No test checks server.json against the registry schema's limits (2025-12-11 schema: description 1..100, title 1..100, name 3..200 + pattern).

data.body: Operator 2026-10-01 approved. Shorten description to <= 100 chars; add a test pinning the registry schema's string limits (description, title, name) so it fails on a local run, not mid-release. Ships with the next patch release (0.1.4) when the operator pushes; re-running publish #34 would republish the same commit.
data.title: server.json fits the MCP Registry schema: description <= 100 chars, pinned by a test (fixes bug B-server-json-description-length)

data.claim: The registry rejected description (251 chars) against ServerDetail.description maxLength 100; no other server.json field breaks a schema string limit
data.falsifier: The 2025-12-11 schema allows >100, or title/name violate their limits
data.probe: curl the $schema URL and list maxLength/minLength/pattern; measure server.json fields
data.question: Why did publish #34's mcp-registry job fail, and which server.json limits does the registry enforce?
